A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gel breaking is suppressed at high particle volume fractions, and the gel dynamics is dominated by the macroscopic deformation at low volume fractions.
, in spite of the apparent simplicity of the system, the microscopic dynamics of colloidal depletion gels is surprisingly rich, and it is still far from being fully understood.
the gel dynamics is governed by the interplay between the microscopic interactions and the macroscopic deformation, which is itself driven by the gravitational stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the microscopic dynamics of short-range depletion gols, although similar in some respects to that of attractive glasses, displays peculiarities which are not shared by any of the known models of the glass transition.

the dynamics of depletion gels is governed by a subtle interplay between the microscopic structure of the gel network and its global compression, which can be fully rationalized within the framework of a simple poroelastic model.
the microscopic dynamics of colloidal glasses can be triggered by gravitational stresses and is thus not restricted to the isothermal compression of dense colloidal suspensions.
